headlines: Bond Yields Kept Climbing And Fed Minutes Showed Another Rate Hike This Year. Stocks Dropped.
Wall Street ends lower, off record highs, as Treasury yields climb

cards.hearing: You may hear that the Fed, which sets short-term interest rates, signaled it could raise rates again before the end of the year, and stocks slipped a little today, Wednesday.
cards.why: When borrowing costs rise, it can nudge what people pay on credit cards, car loans, and other borrowing, so it hits daily life, not just Wall Street.
cards.but: But a single signal about future rate moves is not the same as knowing where the economy lands months from now.
cards.story: Picture a coach announcing at halftime that the team might run a different play later in the game. Fans groan, but the game is not decided yet. The plan still has three quarters left to play out.
say: We saw the Fed's signal, and we are not rewriting your plan off one headline.
One signal about future moves does not decide the whole season.

cards.hearing: You may also hear that the rate on a 30-year mortgage ticked a little higher than last week.
cards.why: That matters because it can change what a monthly house payment looks like for anyone buying or refinancing soon.
cards.but: But rates move up and down over time, and your long-term plan was built to handle that kind of back-and-forth.
cards.story: Picture shopping for a house and the listed price changes a little while you are still saving. Frustrating, sure, but it does not mean you stop saving or give up on buying a home someday.
say: Mortgage rates wiggle. Your plan was built to ride those wiggles.
We don't chase every weekly rate change. We stick with the plan.

cards.hearing: You may hear that stocks had a rough day, pulling back from their recent record highs, with smaller companies falling more than the big ones.
cards.why: When borrowing costs rise, it can cost more for businesses to expand or hire, and that can spook investors in the short run.
cards.but: But pullbacks after record highs are part of how markets normally breathe, not a sign the plan is broken.
cards.story: Think of a hiker who reaches a high ridge, then takes a few steps back down to catch their breath before continuing the climb. The pause does not erase the progress already made.
say: A dip after new highs is normal, not a reason to change course.
We built your plan expecting days like this.
